tools.name: recall
tools.description:
CALL THIS FIRST, before proposing any hypothesis (pre-mortem gate).

Returns ranked past hypotheses/experiments. **Refuted and inconclusive
matches are ranked to the TOP** with a one-line reason they failed and the
diagnostic delta that killed them — so you never silently re-walk a dead end.
Also returns a calibration note if the query touches a diagnostic with a
track record. After reading this, propose a NEW hypothesis (or supersede a
prior one) with a committed prediction.

query.description: Free-text about the idea you're about to try

tools.name: register_tag
tools.description:
Register a tag BEFORE using it. Tags are a fixed vocabulary, like
diagnostics — free-text tagging rots (every session invents a synonym, the
tag connects nothing, and recall silently misses). Idempotent: calling again
MERGES new aliases into the existing tag.

aliases.description: Synonyms that resolve to this tag, e.g. ['causality'] on 'causal-inference'. Absorbing a synonym is how you STOP the vocabulary fragmenting.

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description:
The registered tag vocabulary with usage counts. CALL THIS BEFORE tagging
anything, and reuse an existing tag (or add your wording as its alias)
instead of coining a near-duplicate. `orphan: true` marks a tag used at most
once or confined to one entity kind — it connects nothing and is dead weight.

tools.name: lineage
tools.description:
Ancestry path root → this experiment. The verdict chain along the path is
the research narrative: what was tried, what failed, what was built on it.

tools.name: children
tools.description:
What was tried ON TOP of this experiment. Use it before re-running an
idea — a child may already have explored it.

tools.name: leaves
tools.description:
The research frontier: experiments nothing was built on top of. This is
where to continue work rather than starting a new branch from scratch.

unevaluated_only.description: Only leaves that are still open (dangling work).

tools.name: abort_experiment
tools.description:
Close a run that CRASHED (OOM, exception, timeout) — no measurement, so
NO evidence. Use this instead of inventing a null result: a crash never
enters calibration and leaves the hypothesis retryable. Then start a new
experiment with parent_experiment_id set to this one.

crash_reason.description: The error / why the run died.

tools.name: create_problem
tools.description:
Register an open research question / failure mode. Do this once per
distinct problem. Use `recall` first to check it isn't already logged.

tools.name: get_problem
tools.description: Fetch a single problem by id.

tools.name: update_problem
tools.description:
Amend a problem after evidence changes its framing, and bump updated_at.

Use this when a root cause is found, a problem is re-scoped, or its stated
symptom is no longer true. A problem record outlives the world it described:
once a failure is fixed, an untouched description makes `recall` hand a
future session the confirmed fix AND a contradicting problem statement.

Only the fields you pass are changed. Record what changed via `add_update`
rather than rewriting history — a superseded framing is provenance, and
negative results are first-class here.

`status='resolved'` is gated: at least one hypothesis on this problem must be
CONFIRMED. Resolution is a claim about reality, so it is earned from a
computed verdict, never asserted directly.

status.description: open | resolved | parked. 'resolved' requires a CONFIRMED hypothesis on this problem; use 'parked' to shelve one.

topic_tags.description: Replaces the existing topic tags — call list_tags() first.

problem_tags.description: Replaces the existing problem tags — call list_tags() first.

add_update.description: Append a DATED entry to the problem's update log. Use this instead of gluing an 'UPDATE 2026-xx-xx:' banner onto the description — banners are unsearchable and push the actual problem statement below the fold in every recall result.

target.description: {diagnostic_id, value, note} — the declared GOAL on the primary diagnostic. Declaring it defines the gap that gap_closure_estimate and portfolio() measure against; without a target every improvement is an absolute crumb with no denominator.

tools.name: list_problems
tools.description: List problems, optionally filtered by status {open|resolved|parked} or tags.

tools.name: register_diagnostic
tools.description:
Register a named, fixed, measurable metric. Diagnostics are a DELIBERATE
fixed basis — comparability across experiments is what makes the causal map
possible. Do this before predicting on a metric. Register the NOISE FLOOR as
soon as you can measure it: sign-only verdicts on a noisy metric are draw
luck, and the top autonomous-research runs all measured their noise first.

direction.description: higher_better | lower_better | neutral. Omitted on an EXISTING diagnostic = keep what is registered; only a brand-new one defaults to neutral.

topic_tags.description: Registered topic tags — call list_tags() first.

requires_control.description: Id of a diagnostic that MUST be recorded alongside this one. Use when the raw number is gameable by a config change that improves it while destroying the signal — e.g. an R2 whose control is 'what a trivial predictor already achieves'. record_diagnostics warns (never blocks) if it is missing.

noise_sigma.description: The metric's noise floor: one repeat-run/re-draw sigma. MEASURE it (re-run the same recipe, same seed policy) rather than assuming it. When set, a directionally-correct primary delta inside noise_k*sigma computes as weak_signal instead of supports — signal vs draw luck.

noise_source.description: REQUIRED with noise_sigma: 'measured' | 'assumed'. doctor() flags heavily-used diagnostics still riding an assumption.

tools.name: list_diagnostics
tools.description: List the registered diagnostic basis.

tools.name: register_intervention
tools.description:
Register a named, reusable change (e.g. unfreeze-projector). Reused across
hypotheses so the causal map can attribute deltas to it.

tools.name: list_interventions
tools.description: List registered interventions.

tools.name: propose_hypothesis
tools.description:
Propose an explanation/intervention for a problem. You MUST commit ≥1
`predicted_effect` on a REGISTERED diagnostic BEFORE testing — this is
rejected otherwise. Committing the prediction up front is what turns this log
into a calibration signal. Call `recall` first. To revise a dead end, pass
`supersedes` rather than deleting it. Declare `ambition_class` so the
portfolio can tell breakthrough attempts from crumb-tuning.

predicted_effects.description: REQUIRED ≥1: [{diagnostic_id, direction: up|down|none, magnitude_note}]. The FIRST is the primary prediction the verdict keys off.

supersedes.description: id of a prior hypothesis this one revises

gates.description: PREREGISTERED pass/fail criteria: [{id, description, blocking, mde, diagnostic_id}]. Commit the magnitude, resource or deployment bar HERE, before the run. A directionally-correct result that fails a blocking gate is recorded as `directional_only`, never `supports`. Set `mde` to the smallest effect the run is POWERED to detect: if that gate then fails and |delta| lands under it, the verdict becomes `null` — a powered null, which is evidence AGAINST the lever rather than a near-miss.

ambition_class.description: tuning (knob on an existing mechanism) | mechanism (new component/method) | reframe (change the problem itself). Declare it BEFORE spending compute — portfolio() shows where the budget went per class, and a plateaued problem rejects further 'tuning' without override_reason.

gap_closure_estimate.description: 0..1: if fully confirmed, what share of the problem's REMAINING gap (see its target) this closes. Forces thinking in fractions of the goal, not absolute crumbs.

override_reason.description: Required ONLY for ambition_class='tuning' on a PLATEAUED problem: why more knob-turning is justified (e.g. an old knob under a genuinely new recipe).

tools.name: start_experiment
tools.description:
Begin testing a hypothesis. If `git_ref` is omitted the server reads the
current branch@commit from git HEAD. Reference the external W&B/MLflow run —
this server stores verdicts, not loss curves.

git_ref.description: branch@shortsha; auto-read from HEAD if omitted

parent_experiment_id.description: The experiment this one BUILDS ON. Set it whenever you are iterating on a previous run — it is what makes lineage/children/leaves work and turns a flat list into a search DAG. Omit only for a genuinely fresh line of attack.

tools.name: record_diagnostics
tools.description:
Record before/after values for measured diagnostics. Re-recording the same
diagnostic overwrites it (idempotent). Observed deltas/directions are derived.

tools.name: import_run_report
tools.description:
Ingest a run-report sidecar — integrity hashes (implementation/config/
split/protocol), git sha, exact device, peak VRAM, oom/nonfinite flags —
into the experiment record. Prefer this over retyping hashes into
`config_note`: frontmatter is searchable and auditable, prose is not. If the
report shows a FAILED run it tells you to call abort_experiment instead of
inventing a null result.

report_path.description: Absolute path to the run's report.json

tools.name: record_gate_results
tools.description:
Record outcomes for the gates preregistered on the hypothesis. YOU compute
the gate (paired bootstrap CI, sign-flip test, VRAM ceiling) and report the
outcome plus the numbers that decided it in `evidence`. A gate that was never
preregistered is REJECTED — inventing a criterion after seeing the data is
post-hoc. Required before close_experiment when blocking gates exist.

tools.name: close_experiment
tools.description:
Finalize: compute observed_effects, prediction_match (per-diagnostic +
overall) and the verdict, then propagate the status to the hypothesis. The
verdict is COMPUTED from the primary prediction vs the observation — you
cannot assert 'confirmed'.

Verdicts: supports / refutes / inconclusive / directional_only / **null** /
**weak_signal**. `null` is a POWERED null — the direction nominally matched
but a blocking gate carrying a preregistered `mde` failed and |delta| came in
under it; treated as a refutation of the lever at the committed scale.
`weak_signal` fires when the primary diagnostic carries a registered noise
floor and the delta lands inside k*sigma: a candidate to RE-DRAW, neither a
win to deploy nor a loss to discard.

Also snapshots the run's recipe_fingerprint (interventions + provenance
hashes) — the context this verdict is valid under, which is what makes
reopen_hypothesis honest later. On a negative verdict the response carries
`interpretation_debt`: call interpret_experiment while the context is fresh.

Put artifacts, headline numbers and dead ends in their own fields rather
than compressing them into `notes`. On a positive match it RETURNS a
suggestion to commit your git_ref; it never commits for you.

artifacts.description: Checkpoint/plot/report paths this run produced. Use this instead of pasting paths into `notes` — a path in prose is unreachable by every query.

key_numbers.description: The numbers that decided the run, e.g. {'delta': 0.0003, 'perm_p': 0.65, 'mde': 0.01}. Stored as data so runs can be compared, not re-read.

do_not_retry.description: Specific things a future session must NOT re-run, and why. Surfaced by recall() as its own block — a warning buried in `notes` is one skim away from being repeated on a GPU.

gpu_hours.description: GPU-hours this run burned — the denominator of portfolio(). Without cost, 40 crumb runs and one breakthrough attempt are indistinguishable in the ledger.

tools.name: interpret_experiment
tools.description:
Record WHAT A CLOSED EXPERIMENT MEANS — the act of analysis the verdict
alone is not. Call it right after close_experiment (the response reminds you
via `interpretation_debt`), or later once several runs make the picture
clear. recall() surfaces the lesson instead of a machine string; doctor()
reports closed-but-uninterpreted experiments as debt. Overwrite freely — a
better interpretation replaces a worse one.

lesson.description: 1-3 sentences a future session can act on. What does this result MEAN — not what happened (the verdict already says that). Indexed by recall, so write it for retrieval.

failure_mode.description: REQUIRED for negative verdicts: claim_false | mechanism_wrong | test_invalid | noise | execution_bug | recipe_conditional. A refute from a broken capture and a refute of the idea are different objects — the taxonomy is what keeps them distinct.

transfers_to.description: Other hypothesis ids this lesson bears on — one post-mortem pruning across the DAG.

tools.name: reopen_hypothesis
tools.description:
Flag a refuted/inconclusive hypothesis as a STALE NEGATIVE — a negative
result is a fact about (claim × recipe), not about the claim, and this makes
that explicit when the recipe drifts. NOT a rewrite: verdicts, experiments
and lineage survive; the status flips to `stale_negative` with dated
provenance. The actual re-test still goes through propose_hypothesis(
supersedes=...) with a fresh committed prediction. Re-opening old negatives
under a new recipe is literally how records get taken.

reason.description: WHAT changed since the refutation: new checkpoint, different capture, an intervention left the stack. 'I want to retry' is not a recipe change.

changed_context.description: Optional detail of the drift (old vs new recipe)

tools.name: progress
tools.description:
Compiled state of one problem: primary-diagnostic trajectory across all
experiments, verdict counts, plateau status (last-N-without-supports),
stale negatives, interpretation debt, and the current synthesis. This is the
raw material for synthesize_problem — the MCP compiles, you interpret.

tools.name: synthesize_problem
tools.description:
Write the problem's ## Synthesis — the difference between a knowledge
base and a junk pile. A problem with a stack of closed experiments and no
synthesis forces every future session to re-derive the state of knowledge
from raw records. Re-synthesize after every batch of experiments; call
progress() first for the compiled material.

synthesis.description: The problem's CURRENT state of knowledge: what we now believe / what is ruled out / open questions. Overwrites the previous synthesis (it is a state, not a log).

tools.name: portfolio
tools.description:
Where the compute went, by ambition class (tuning / mechanism / reframe /
undeclared): experiments, gpu-hours, supports, declared gap closure, and
supports-per-gpu-hour. Makes crumb-optimization visible — 31 tuning runs
for +3% next to 1 reframe for +9% is a decision-forcing sentence the raw
log can never say. Data only; the decision stays with you.

tools.name: research_brief
tools.description:
Compile the vault's accumulated knowledge into a ready deep-research
query: problem state + gap, plateau flag, dead ideas with their lessons,
rule-outs, and the full already-read paper EXCLUSION list. Feed the returned
`query` to perplexity_research, verify arXiv ids via the arxiv MCP, then
add_paper() the keepers and cite them in the next mechanism/reframe
hypothesis. This is the plateau escape hatch: the literature is the edge a
sandboxed harness doesn't have — but only if each sweep is incremental
instead of re-finding last month's reading list.

tools.name: add_paper
tools.description:
Add an external reference (metadata + key claims). Cite it from hypotheses
to ground your rationale.

tools.name: link_paper
tools.description: Link a paper to a problem or hypothesis (adds a cites edge).

tools.name: causal_map
tools.description:
Aggregated intervention → Δdiagnostic subgraph across all experiments in
scope: what has ever moved a diagnostic, in which direction, how often, by how
much. A mini meta-analysis of your own runs. Scope by problem_id or tag.

READ THE ATTRIBUTION FIELD. An edge marked `confounded` means the intervention
was NEVER applied alone — its delta cannot be separated from whatever it was
bundled with, and it is not independent evidence no matter how many
experiments back it. `n_isolated_experiments` is the honest count and
`isolated_mean_delta` the honest effect. Each edge also carries the `verdicts`
of its contributing experiments: a green arrow built purely from
`inconclusive` or `directional_only` runs is not a finding.

min_verdict.description: Only count effects from experiments at or above this verdict strength: refutes < inconclusive < directional_only < supports. Use 'supports' to see only edges backed by runs that actually passed their gates.

tools.name: rule_out
tools.description:
Record a claim eliminated by direct measurement, WITHOUT a formal hypothesis.

Use for cheap probes that killed an idea: not everything that dies deserves a
hypothesis record, but it must not die in prose either. Rule-outs are surfaced
at the TOP of `recall` for their problem, so the next session cannot miss them
the way a paragraph buried in a long description gets missed. Reversible via
`retract_rule_out` when new evidence reopens the question.

claim.description: The claim being ELIMINATED, stated so a future session recognises it if re-proposed.

method.description: HOW it was eliminated — the probe/analysis. Required: a rule-out with no method is a rumour.

evidence.description: The numbers that killed it. Required.

tools.name: list_rule_outs
tools.description:
List claims already eliminated by measurement. Check this before proposing
a hypothesis — re-testing a ruled-out claim burns GPU time on a known answer.

tools.name: retract_rule_out
tools.description:
Reopen a previously ruled-out claim. Additive — the record survives, marked
retracted, so both the original measurement and the correction stay auditable.

tools.name: register_runbook
tools.description:
Queue a runnable plan against a problem — the answer to 'what next?'.

A runbook is INTENT, never evidence: it holds the prompt, its preconditions and
the gates it should commit to. The prediction is still committed through
`propose_hypothesis` at run time, so a queued plan can never be mistaken for a
preregistration. Use this instead of keeping the queue in a repo file that
drifts out of sync with the vault.

prompt.description: A SELF-CONTAINED instruction a fresh session can execute with no memory of this chat: restate the context, the evidence and the thresholds.

gates.description: Gate ids this arm SHOULD commit to at run time.

tools.name: list_runbooks
tools.description:
List queued plans, lowest priority number first. Ask 'what should I run next
on this problem?' with status='queued'.

tools.name: update_runbook
tools.description:
Advance a runbook: queued → running → done/abandoned, and link the hypothesis
it produced so intent and evidence stay connected. Record WHY via `note`.

status.description: queued | running | done | abandoned. Marking 'done' REQUIRES a hypothesis_id — work that recorded no hypothesis is 'abandoned', not done.

note.description: Append a dated entry to this runbook's log — WHY the status changed, what blocked it. Strongly encouraged when abandoning: a plan that vanishes without a reason is one a future session re-queues.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description:
Vault health check: find records whose STATUS no longer matches reality.

Reports, without changing anything: problems still `open` that already have a
confirmed hypothesis; hypotheses rotting in `proposed`/`testing`; experiments
left open; near-duplicate experiments started minutes apart on the same
hypothesis (the fingerprint of a double `start_experiment`); runbooks queued
against resolved/missing problems; orphan and probable-duplicate tags.

This matters because `recall` hands a future session the framing these
records assert — a problem that was answered months ago but still reads
`open` actively misleads it. Every finding names the tool that fixes it;
nothing is auto-repaired, because a heuristic that silently closed records
would corrupt the log worse than a stale status does.

stale_days.description: Age in days past which a proposed/testing hypothesis, an open experiment or a queued runbook is reported as stale.

tools.name: merge_tags
tools.description:
Fold a duplicate tag into its canonical form across the WHOLE vault.

The vocabulary could only ever grow, so near-synonyms like `contrastive` /
`contrastive-loss` split one concept's evidence across two labels and
`recall` missed whichever half a past session did not happen to type.

This rewrites every entity that used `source`, then keeps `source` as an
ALIAS of `into` — so historical spellings still resolve and no provenance is
destroyed. Both tags must be on the same axis. Run `doctor()` to find
candidates.

source.description: The duplicate tag to fold away.

tools.name: calibration
tools.description:
Prediction-accuracy report: the fraction of experiments where predicted
direction == observed direction. Answers 'where is my intuition
miscalibrated?'. Scope by diagnostic, tag, or intervention.

tools.name: reindex
tools.description:
Rebuild the disposable SQLite index from the markdown vault (files are
truth). Safe to call anytime; produces identical query results.

ruled_out.claim: AIST++ can supply block A, the shared audio->movement skeleton. ELIMINATED for this corpus. What varies between AIST++ tracks is the dance GENRE, not the acoustics, and the movement follows the genre.
ruled_out.method: Direct replication of Burger et al. 2013's stimulus-level design on all 60 AIST++ tracks: one row per track, movement averaged over every dancer and frame, audio averaged over the track, bootstrap CIs over tracks; then the same correlations with genre and tempo partialled out; then the share of between-track movement variance explained by the genre label alone; then a check of whether audio can recover genre at all.
ruled_out.evidence: Not one published correlation replicates, and several invert. Pulse clarity -> quantity of motion: Burger +0.62, here -0.078 (CI [-0.341, +0.169]). Low-band flux -> head speed: +0.73 vs -0.102. High-band flux -> hand speed: +0.65 vs -0.321. High-band flux -> hand spread: +0.57 vs -0.396 (CI excludes zero, wrong sign). The audio features do vary across the corpus (CV 0.16 to 0.68), so this is not a range restriction. The explanation is the corpus design: the genre label alone explains 0.835 of between-track variance in quantity of motion, 0.916 in centre-of-mass speed, 0.879 in vertical bounce amplitude and 0.955 in footfall rate. With genre and tempo partialled out, every audio-movement correlation collapses to between -0.18 and +0.21 with CIs spanning zero. AIST++ is choreographed street dance whose music was chosen to match the style, so the arrow runs genre -> both music and movement; Burger's participants moved freely to varied music, where the arrow runs music -> movement. The shared component is real and highly reliable (split-half up to 0.94 for footfall rate) — it is simply not acoustic. Block A therefore needs free-dancing data; the Oslo club-dancing EDM mocap (Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0) is the corpus for it.

ruled_out.claim: AIST++ needs a per-track audio-motion sync offset: the dance is period-locked but phase-random against the music because each track's motion clock is shifted by an unknown constant. ELIMINATED.
ruled_out.method: Fit one offset per music id as the R-weighted circular mean of per-clip footfall beat phases, using only half of each track's clips; validate on the held-out half, then test the SAME offset on a channel it was not fitted to (vertical bounce minima). A genuine clock offset shifts every channel of a clip equally, so it must transfer.
ruled_out.evidence: The hypothesis looked strong: clips of one track agreed on a phase across different choreographies and dancers (concentration R = 0.59), the per-track estimate was split-half stable (r = 0.83), and on held-out clips the correction lifted footfall beat alignment from +0.019 (CI [-0.006, +0.044], i.e. chance) to +0.128 (CI [+0.103, +0.153]) — above the audio beat-trigger baseline's +0.101. It still fails the transfer test: on vertical bounce minima of held-out clips the raw signal is already aligned (+0.0382, CI [+0.0230, +0.0541]) and applying the footfall-fitted offset DESTROYS that alignment (+0.0081, CI [-0.0068, +0.0228]). There is no missing clock offset. What the corpus actually contains is a channel-specific phase: vertical bounce sits on the beat with no correction (the Toiviainen 2010 / Burger 2013 prediction), while footfall phase belongs to the choreography, which in street dance is routinely off the beat. Provenance: lightsem/data/sync.py, kept as a documented refutation with the fitting code intact.

ruled_out.claim: The 'Just Dance / pose-as-free-encoder' hack works as proposed: dancer kinetic energy KE(t)=sum_j||dP_j/dt||^2 is a valid dense ground-truth signal for light DIMMER at beat/frame resolution, and jerk peaks are a valid trigger for STROBE/color-snaps, such that a model trained audio->pose->DMX learns choreographer-encoded musical semantics that plain FFT/envelope features do not carry. ALSO ELIMINATED: (a) that the near-zero beat-scale agreement is an artifact of a fixed sync lag between clips; (b) that it is explained by the dancers performing different choreographies; (c) that it is a Pearson amplitude artifact that would disappear if measured as event TIMING instead.
ruled_out.method:
exp-lightsem-p1p2-20260807. Two pure-CPU probes on AIST++ (real licensed paired 3D motion + music: 1408 sequences, 60 tracks, keypoints3d.zip from google/aistplusplus_dataset v1.0 + AIST audio wav.zip). NO scraping needed -- the sketch's premise that this data must be pirated from YouTube is false.

PROBE 1 (probe1_pose_vs_audio.py, 263 usable sequences, 12 music ids): computed the sketch's exact KE formula on root-relative 3D keypoints; measured (M1) Pearson r vs librosa RMS/onset envelope at 4 smoothing timescales; (M2) RidgeCV R^2 from a 28-dim audio stack (RMS, onset, flux, centroid, flatness, spectral contrast, 20 MFCC) -> KE with GroupKFold BY MUSIC; (M3) THE CEILING -- r(KE_dancerA, KE_dancerB) for the SAME music, different dancer (1574 pairs). M3 upper-bounds any audio->pose model, since audio cannot predict what differs between two dancers hearing the same track.

PROBE 2 (probe2_artifact_controls.py, 231 sequences, 115 same-choreography/different-dancer pairs vs 1373 different-choreography pairs) -- three artifact controls: (A1) replaced zero-lag Pearson with MAX cross-correlation over +-1.0s of lag; (A2) split pairs into SAME-choreography (reproducibility ceiling / noise floor) vs DIFFERENT-choreography; (A3) abandoned Pearson entirely and measured event TIMING -- jerk-peak 'hit' events matched at +-70ms, F1 vs a rate-matched uniform-random null, plus motion-hits vs the librosa beat grid.
ruled_out.evidence:
M1 r(KE, RMS envelope): 0.031 @0.1s, 0.080 @0.5s, 0.261 @2.0s, 0.653 @8.0s (r_onset nearly identical: 0.031/0.108/0.283/0.667). The 'KE->dimmer' formula IS an audio envelope at phrase scale and is uncorrelated with audio at beat scale.

M2 audio->KE Ridge R^2 (GroupKFold by music, so held-out track): 0.0019 @0.1s, 0.0050 @0.5s, -0.0254 @2.0s, -0.0694 @8.0s. Generalises to a NEW track at essentially zero; negative at the very scale where within-track correlation was 0.65 -- i.e. the 8s correlation is per-track offset structure, not a transferable audio->motion law.

M3 inter-dancer ceiling r (same music, different dancer, n=1574): 0.024 @0.1s, 0.047 @0.5s, 0.132 @2.0s, 0.495 @8.0s => R^2_ceiling 0.0006 / 0.0022 / 0.0174 / 0.2449. At beat scale the ceiling is ~0: two humans dancing the same track do NOT agree on instantaneous kinetic energy.

ARTIFACT CONTROLS (probe 2) -- all three rejected:
A1 lag correction raises absolute values but does not change the conclusion: max-xcorr over +-1s gives 0.313 @0.1s, 0.366 @0.5s, 0.466 @2.0s, 0.812 @8.0s. The zero-lag reading was partly a sync artifact, but the timescale gradient survives.
A2 THE DECISIVE CONTROL: SAME-choreography vs DIFFERENT-choreography pairs are statistically indistinguishable at every timescale -- 0.313 vs 0.290 @0.1s, 0.366 vs 0.354 @0.5s, 0.466 vs 0.464 @2.0s, 0.812 vs 0.842 @8.0s (n=115 vs 250; gaps far inside the +-0.14-0.36 spreads). Two dancers performing THE SAME choreography to the same music agree no better than two dancers performing DIFFERENT choreographies. So the measured agreement carries no choreography-specific information at all; it is generic 'a human is moving to ~120 BPM music' structure.
A3 event-timing rescue fails too: motion-hit F1 at +-70ms = 0.250 same-choreo vs 0.191 random null (lift +0.060) and 0.223 vs 0.186 (lift +0.037) diff-choreo. Motion hits vs the librosa BEAT GRID: F1=0.116 vs 0.103 null, lift +0.013, n=209, mean tempo 119.8 BPM -- dancers' sharp movements are barely above chance at landing on the beat.

CONCLUSION: the pose detour is ill-posed at exactly the resolution the light needs (strobe/color-snap at 0.1-0.5s) and redundant with a 3-line librosa envelope at the resolution where it does correlate (8s). Per multimodal-ai lecture 08, cross-modal transfer moves only REDUNDANT information; here the fine-scale component is not redundant, it is dancer-idiosyncratic, so no audio model can recover it and any single dancer is an arbitrary ground truth. Additionally the motivating premise is superseded: Skip-BART (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2506.01482) already learns audio->light from REAL lighting-engineer demonstrations, with dataset RPMC-L2 released CC-BY-4.0 -- strictly better-posed supervision than a dancer proxy, and legally clean versus scraping YouTube (which the ToS prohibits outright).

ruled_out.claim: A causal temporal encoder over openl3 audio embeddings can predict the RPMC-L2 stage-lighting scene vector (6-dim HSV summary), i.e. a trained macro layer can replace the hand-written rule table by regressing audio -> absolute lighting state.
ruled_out.method: Marginal-contribution test on per-song-centred targets, held-out songs. (1) Ridge fits for audio-only, persistence-only (y's own lags 0.1-4.0 s), and AR+audio; the audio claim stands or falls on AR+audio minus AR, not on audio's absolute score. (2) A 2.36M-param causal transformer trained 40 epochs as the strong-model control. (3) A lag-shift control: audio-light correlation recomputed with y shifted +-30 s WITHIN each song, since real frame-level coupling must peak at lag 0 while slow co-drift does not. Split is by song (hash), so no venue appears in both train and test.
ruled_out.evidence:
Refuted by a marginal-contribution test, not by a weak model.

SETUP: 140 songs, 126,332 frames @10 Hz, split BY SONG (99/23/18). Target is
the per-song-CENTRED scene vector (35-65% of raw variance is between-song
venue palette, which is given, not predicted). Metric R2_within on held-out songs.

TRAINED MODEL (2,359,769 params, causal, 40 epochs, RTX 5070):
  test R2_within (now)   = -0.0071
  best epoch             = 0 (before learning anything)
  train loss 0.1554 -> 0.0418 while val R2 fell -0.004 -> -0.445 (memorisation)

BASELINES (all below the zero point):
  per-song mean oracle   = -0.0000  <- zero point
  best fair linear       = -0.1091

CEILING PROBE (the decisive measurement):
  audio only             = -0.1091
  persistence only (AR)  = +0.7083
  AR + audio             = +0.7035
  audio's marginal gain  = -0.0049   <- NEGATIVE

Lighting is ~71% predictable from its own past 0.1-4.0 s, with NO audio.
Adding 512 audio dims on top of that does not help.

TIME-SHIFT CONTROL: correlation of audio vs light, y shifted within-song:
  lag -30s 0.27325 | lag 0s 0.14104 | lag +30s 0.17044
Peak at lag -30s, MINIMUM near zero. Real frame-level coupling
must peak at lag 0. This is slow co-drift over minutes, not coupling.

ruled_out.claim: AIST Dance DB audio is a usable corpus for validating EDM structure detection and anticipatory (build-up -> drop) lighting control. ELIMINATED. AIST tracks are short, loudness-normalised dance loops whose energy dynamic range is ~5x too small to contain the build-up/drop structure the anticipation layer exists to detect. Also eliminated as the SOLE explanation of the weak first result: 'the segmentation/anticipation detector is broken' -- a synthetic control proves the detector localises real drops to <1 s.
ruled_out.method:
Two-hypothesis discrimination with a SYNTHETIC CONTROL SIGNAL. The first anticipation run on 5 AIST tracks gave recall 0.000 on 3/5, and on the one track scoring 0.800 the rate-matched random baseline was 0.625 (i.e. no skill). Two competing explanations were separated rather than assumed: H1 detector broken; H2 corpus has no structure.

probe_control_synthetic.py synthesises EDM-shaped audio (kick on the beat, rising riser + amplitude ramp through an 8 s build, wide bright drop section, quiet breakdown) with drops at KNOWN times 16.0 s and 36.0 s, and runs the IDENTICAL librosa laplacian-segmentation + labelling + anticipation pipeline over it. Energy dynamic range (RMS p90/p10, std/mean) is measured on the synthetic track and on 10 real AIST tracks for direct comparison.

probe_anticipation_baselines.py then prices the anticipation claim against THREE nulls rather than a bare number: (1) rate-matched uniform-random cues, 500 draws; (2) a metronome cue process at the same rate, 20 phases; (3) a NULL TRACK of steady-state audio with no drops, to expose a trigger-happy detector. Scoring uses precision and nearest-cue lead time, because recall saturates for every method once the credit window is wide.
ruled_out.evidence:
=== ENERGY DYNAMIC RANGE (the decisive contrast) ===
  synthetic EDM control : RMS p90/p10 = 18.27   std/mean = 0.726
  AIST median of 10     : RMS p90/p10 =  3.76   std/mean ~ 0.45
  per-track AIST p90/p10: mBR0 6.45, mBR1 4.16, mBR2 3.45, mBR3 4.06,
                          mBR4 4.79, mBR5 5.42, mHO0 2.95, mHO1 2.68,
                          mHO2 2.86, mHO3 3.24
AIST segment energies sit inside a 0.475-0.518 band on a 0-1 normalised scale -- essentially no build-up/drop contour exists.

=== H1 REFUTED: the detector works on audio that HAS structure ===
After fixing a labelling defect (below), drop localisation error against the known synthetic drops is 0.44 s and 0.57 s.
Anticipation on the synthetic track, scored honestly:
  REAL      precision 1.000   nearest-lead 2.78 s +- 0.08 s
  RANDOM    precision 0.495 +- 0.208   nearest-lead 4.36 s +- 2.48 s
  METRONOME precision 0.500 +- 0.106   nearest-lead 3.37 s +- 1.66 s
  precision z vs random = +2.42
The lead-time STD is the sharpest discriminator: 0.08 s real vs 2.48 s random. It is not merely hitting the window, it is hitting a consistent phase of the build.

=== NULL TRACK CONTROL (not trigger-happy) ===
On steady-state drop-free audio the cue rate collapses 0.146 Hz -> 0.021 Hz. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS, NOT HIDDEN: the labeller still tags 3 spurious 'drop' segments on that audio, so boundary detection is solid while the functional labeller is the weak link.

=== WHY RECALL WAS THE WRONG HEADLINE ===
At 7 cues / 48 s with a 12 s credit window, rate-matched random cues reach 0.816 recall vs the real detector's 0.875 -- a margin near zero. Recall saturates and cannot separate methods; precision and lead-time concentration can, and do (z = +2.42).

=== THREE REAL BUGS THE CONTROL EXPOSED (none visible from AIST) ===
1. librosa.util.sync emits one MORE column than beat frames, so a cluster-change index could equal len(beat_times) -> IndexError crash.
2. QUANTILE labelling mislabels loud segments: a 0.613-energy segment was labelled 'breakdown' while the track max was 0.620, because it sat below the 0.66 quantile. Localisation error was 3.23 s / 6.66 s. Fixed by labelling RELATIVE TO THE TRACK'S OWN ENERGY RANGE plus an explicit drop-follows-build-up rule -> 0.44 s / 0.57 s.
3. THE METRIC PUNISHED BETTER ANTICIPATION (see the companion rule-out).

=== CONSEQUENCE ===
AIST stays correct for pose/choreography work and is fine as a RENDERING input, but structure-detection and anticipation claims must be validated on EDM-98 / EDM-CUE (arXiv 2603.08759, HF disco-eth/edm-cue), NOT yet downloaded. Any anticipation number quoted on AIST audio is uninformative about the mechanism.

ruled_out.claim: Segmentation-first (beat-synchronous / structural-section alignment) rescues the pose-as-intermediate-representation idea at the resolution a light cue needs. Specifically: that the near-zero fixed-window beat-scale agreement was purely a methodology artifact of using non-semantic fixed windows, and that once you segment before aligning, dancer motion becomes a usable dense supervision signal for DMX dimmer/strobe.
ruled_out.method:
probe3b_segment_first.py + probe4_significance.py, prompted by re-reading the multimodal-ai skill (MIT MAS.S60 lecture 06, Connections & Alignment). The skill's design rule 'when modalities are continuous with no natural elements, solve segmentation BEFORE alignment' and its pitfall #4 ('applying discrete-alignment methods to continuous data ... pretending fixed windows are semantic units is a silent correctness bug') identified that probes 1 and 2 had committed exactly that error: they smoothed with FIXED windows (0.1/0.5/2/8s) and correlated frame-wise.

probe3 v1 had a data bug: AIST++ pose clips are median 8.7s while audio tracks are 30-51s, so computing beats/sections over the whole track and requiring >=20 valid beats inside a clip discarded nearly all pairs (same-choreo n=0). Diagnosed with diag_durations.py; probe3b fixes it by clipping the audio analysis to each sequence's own duration and segmenting within that span (271 usable sequences, 136 same-choreo pairs, 1550 diff-choreo pairs, 12 tracks).

Three segmentation-first tests replacing fixed windows: T1 beat-synchronous KE aggregation (librosa.util.sync over the beat grid) + beat-sync audio->KE RidgeCV with GroupKFold by music; T2 independent structural segmentation of the audio (beat-sync MFCC+chroma -> agglomerative) and of the pose stream, then boundary-matching F1 at +-0.5s against a rate-matched random null, with the inter-dancer boundary F1 as the ceiling; T3 section-level mean KE using the audio's own section boundaries as the shared abstracted unit.

probe4 then tested whether the resulting SAME>DIFF gap is real given that pairs are NOT independent (each dancer/track recurs across many pairs): cluster-aware permutation shuffling the SAME/DIFF label WITHIN each track (10000 perms), bootstrap over TRACKS as the independent unit (10000 resamples), track-level bootstrap CI on the boundary-F1 lift, and Cohen's d.
ruled_out.evidence:
PARTIAL RETRACTION OF THE FIXED-WINDOW FINDING -- segmentation DID change the qualitative result, and the earlier probe-2 claim 'same-choreo agrees no better than diff-choreo' is now shown to be an artifact of fixed windows:

probe3b beat-synchronous inter-dancer r: SAME choreo +0.131 +-0.320 (n=136) vs DIFF choreo -0.007 +-0.277 (n=400). Under fixed windows (probe2) these were 0.366 vs 0.354 -- indistinguishable. So natural musical units DO expose choreography-specific structure that fixed windows hid.

Significance (probe4, cluster-aware because pairs are non-independent):
- S1 permutation, labels shuffled WITHIN each track, 10000 perms: observed gap +0.1377, null +0.0001 +-0.0489, two-sided p=0.0041. SIGNIFICANT.
- S2 bootstrap over the 12 TRACKS as independent units: gap 95% CI [+0.088, +0.194], excludes 0. Cohen's d = +0.476 (moderate).
- S3 structural boundaries: pose-derived section boundaries vs audio-derived boundaries F1=0.462 vs random null 0.331, inter-dancer ceiling 0.500 => 77.1% OF CEILING. Lift-over-null 95% CI [+0.079, +0.184], excludes 0.

SO: real, statistically significant, non-artifactual shared structure EXISTS at the segmented/structural level.

BUT THE ENGINEERING CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED, on magnitude not on existence:
- S4: beat-sync inter-dancer r=+0.131 => R^2=0.0171. Even a PERFECT audio->pose model explains at most 1.71% of another dancer's beat-level kinetic energy. The ceiling is real but tiny.
- audio->KE Ridge on a HELD-OUT track, beat-synchronous, GroupKFold by music: R^2 = -0.0089 (N=5274) -- still negative, i.e. worse than predicting the mean. Segmentation did not make the mapping learnable across tracks.
- The one place pose is genuinely informative is STRUCTURAL BOUNDARIES (77% of ceiling) -- but that is exactly what dedicated MIR structure models (All-In-One, Beat This!, EDMFormer) already provide directly from audio, without a dancer, without pose estimation, and without the legal problem.

NET: the ORIGINAL rule-out stands on its operative claim (KE as a dense beat-resolution DMX supervision signal is not viable: R^2 ceiling 1.7%, cross-track generalisation negative). The SUPPORTING ARGUMENT from probe 2 ('no choreography-specific information exists at all') is RETRACTED as a fixed-window artifact -- such information does exist, it is just far too weak to carry a lighting cue, and the useful part of it (structure) is better obtained straight from audio.

results.statement: A learned group-effects decoder (Anton's mixture of light: a shared type-masked head on the frozen trunk and operator head emitting per-group intensity envelope, palette, effect id, rate in beats, phase spread and density, expanded to DMX by a deterministic effects engine) trained on authored light through a differentiable histogram renderer with random-rig dropout beats the hand-written conductor on Value- and onset-matched held-out songs: FID vs conductor beats a shuffled-donor control by > 2x, BAS is not lower without more onsets, raters prefer it on 'fits the music' with a CI excluding 50% at n >= 20, and it transfers to an unseen patch better than channel-copy.
results.why_it_failed: refuted: predicted fid-light-kinetic down, observed up (Δ +886.079)

results.statement: Light derived from real dance motion by a fixed body-following mapping (conductor v0) is musically timed: its visible accents align to the beat better than the same accents circularly shifted, and the distribution of its delta features is separable from a structure-destroying null.
results.why_it_failed: refuted [mechanism_wrong]: The idea survives, the assumed mechanism does not. The hypothesis assumed a dancing body carries the musics timing into the light. It carries the PERIOD (footfall Rayleigh R 0.55, median z 5.2 per clip) but not the PHASE, which belongs to the choreography and is therefore not in the audio and not learnable from it. Dance supplies WHAT the light does (how much, how wide, which side, how deep the bounce, when the look changes); audio supplies WHEN the transients land. Evidence that this is a fix and not a retreat: the hybrid conductor built on that split scores +0.124 (CI [+0.114,+0.135]) against +0.094 (CI [+0.083,+0.106]) for the audio-only beat trigger, while staying close to the dance-derived look (FID 43 to the oracle vs 794 to the beat trigger). Stage 1 trains block A as regression on dance-derived envelopes and block B as a hazard conditioned on audio beat phase, never an absolute event phase copied from the dancer. Stage 0c must compare the HYBRID against the beat trigger, brightness-matched; comparing the motion-only oracle would test a straw man this experiment already shows is mistimed.

results.statement: Section-level intent belongs on the conductor, not in the per-frame model: an audio-only offline planner that writes scene family, palette, intensity class, strobe density and transition type per section onto the conductor / engine knobs (one bar ahead allowed) beats the no-planner model and a shuffled-section-plan control on FID_light and on the human 'feels intentionally structured' question, with paired Light-BAS not lower. H-C refuted section channels as per-frame input; this is the untested lever.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted fid-light-kinetic down, observed down (Δ -5613.94)

results.statement: A look sampler that HOLDS its sampled look between cues fired by the calibrated look-change hazard (refractory 2 s, rate matched to the corpus) reproduces the authored corpora's look-transition statistics better than a per-frame sampler and than a shuffled donor, and lands on the beat no worse than the hand-written conductor at no higher onset density.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted cue-transition-distance down, observed down (Δ -2.012)

results.statement: A beat-conditioned A/B/C sequence model with correct world aiming and independent emitted-light checks will produce more physically valid visible movement than the current no-clock body-v2 prototype while retaining measurable nonbeat audio control.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive [recipe_conditional]: World-target geometry repairs emitted-light visibility (1.0 vs 0.0); old weights with the same map also reach 1.0. The new recipe does not establish musical motion control: only 0.025 of40songs pass same-beat spectral-response/noise criteria, and A alignment advantage is -0.2130; report event selectivity's separate pass without hiding these failures. A future motion-control change must be evaluated on emitted trajectories with fixed rhythm and paired noise, retaining local timing checks.

results.statement: The Just Dance background, with coach and UI masked, is a designed light show whose scene changes and palette shifts are predictable from audio in the same way a human operator's are on RPMC-L2: audio's marginal lift over the rhythm-of-past-changes baseline clears +0.09 with z > 3 on held-out songs, and the time-shift control peaks at 0.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted event-ap-lift-audio-marginal up, observed up (Δ +1.6902)

results.statement: A factorised audio-light critic trained with time-shift, other-song AND beat-trigger negatives on bar-synchronous tokens learns something beyond beat and loudness: it separates real authored light from beat-trigger light on held-out songs above chance, its best-of-8 ranking over rectified-flow samples changes when the critic is projected to its nearest additive model, and best-of-8 beats random-of-8 on human 'fits the music'. Without the beat-trigger negative it collapses to a beat detector and rewards the mode the model already occupies.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted critic-pair-accuracy up, observed up (Δ +0.393)

results.statement: Authored hobby/game light shows are lighting corpora, not tempo corpora: on xLights free .xsq sequences (where the song is on disk) and Beat Saber lightshow maps, audio predicts the group-level event stream and envelopes on held-out shows with AP_audio - AP_time-shift >= +0.15 and AP_audio >= AP_beat-trigger + 0.05, causal and offline. A corpus that fails stays out of every loss.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted event-ap-lift-audio-marginal up, observed up (Δ +0.3553)

results.statement: Dance is not a category error for light. Light derived from real dance motion through the hybrid conductor (dance envelopes, audio-phased transients), brightness-matched against a 30-line audio beat trigger on the same music, is preferred by a blind rater on at least one of two questions: 'which is on the music?' and 'which looks like a lighting engineer did it?'. If the beat trigger wins both, block C (the sampled style residual) leaves the product.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted human-preference-winrate up, observed up (Δ +0.35)

results.statement: Feeding the group decoder the hazard features of its OWN emitted cues (teacher-forced in training, autoregressive in 1 s blocks at inference) raises its held-out cue-timing lift above the audio-only decoder on Just Dance visual and RPMC-L2, recovering part of the margin the with-hazard operator head holds (3.17x vs 2.35x on JD); decoder size alone does not.

data.description: Accepted representation-first implementation 2026-09-10. Build convincing music-driven stage lighting. Music is the only playback input; an internal generated skeleton/motion sequence is explicitly allowed. Hybrid measured audio dynamics may control brightness and movement intensity. Quiet passages must remain visible but restrained. Establish clean motion-source and temporal-codec quality before audio training. Prior human review rejects flashing/juggling reconstructions and excessive Shpongle movement; only the incumbent audio-to-descriptions-to-pose path is currently visually convincing. Glare improvement is useful but does not establish visible head-brightness dynamics. Exploration seed0; confirm only qualifying finalist and matched baseline at seed1. Accelerated BF16/compile/prefetch in matched arms, no earlier 2–3h ceiling. Historical nulls and gates remain valid.

STATE OF KNOWLEDGE — 2026-09-08, continuation audit + incremental primary-source literature review.

Scope: pre-rendered audio -> stage lighting; whole-song context allowed; dance is training supervision only. The old causal-only/no-experiments synthesis is superseded. Current learned renderer uses the descriptor/event/style model with ConductorHybrid. Stage9 GroupEngine and generic CLI are separate entry points.

Strong synchronization scores can coexist with poor aesthetics. Historical supports/directional-only records are not blanket product gates. GroupDecoder is not a faithful Skip-BART/SeqLight implementation: it omits autoregressive light tokens, histogram targets and learned temporal decomposition. Existing recurrence analysis retains boundaries but not motif memory. Per-bar regression therefore does not rule out explicit motif reuse.

New literature adds implementable SLS/EUBO preference acquisition, editable light-object layers (Glow with the Flow), explicit hierarchical/repetition representations, Beat This timing models and Raveform annotation access. RPMC is video-derived colour supervision, not professional DMX logs; no newly usable authored-control corpus was established.

data.description:
Mapping music/audio to stage lighting control (DMX, hue/value/intensity, strobe, beam). Covers rule-based sound-to-light (FFT/beatgrid triggers) and learned/generative approaches (Skip-BART, SeqLight).

*Axis:* `topic`

Design and validation of metrics: Light-BAS (beat alignment of light kinematics), FID over light features, diversity, collapse rate, human pairwise preference, and the nulls (metronome, circular shift, split-half) each one must be priced against.

*Axis:* `topic`

Treating the target as a distribution to SAMPLE from (diffusion, flow matching, diffusion forcing, VQ+AR) rather than a function to regress. Use when p(y|x) is multi-modal and per-frame MSE collapses to the conditional mean.

*Axis:* `topic`

Music-conditioned dance/motion generation (EDGE, FlowerDance, InfiniteDance, DiscoForcing) and its datasets (AIST++, FineDance, InfiniteDance). In LightSem the generated dancer is a LATENT intermediate: present at train time, sampled at test time.

*Axis:* `topic`

Human pose / skeletal keypoint time series as a modality (2D/3D keypoints, kinetic energy, jerk, motion events). Includes dance motion and pose used as an intermediate representation.

*Axis:* `topic`
*Axis:* `topic`

Empirical music-psychology literature on how audio features drive spontaneous body movement across many people (Burger/Toiviainen/Luck Jyvaskyla mocap, Solberg & Jensenius club EDM, groove research). Source of the shared-vs-personal split that defines LightSem's target blocks.

*Axis:* `topic`

The chosen supervision target is not a function of the available input: multiple equally valid targets exist for the same input (one-to-many mapping), so any single recorded target is an arbitrary draw. Training against it caps achievable performance at the inter-annotator/inter-performer agreement ceiling, and a model appearing to 'fail' may simply be hitting that ceiling. Diagnosed by measuring agreement between independent targets for identical input before modelling.

*Axis:* `problem`
*Axis:* `problem`

Strictly causal, bounded-latency streaming inference (audio-in to DMX-out). Covers online beat tracking, causal audio encoders, diffusion forcing, teacher->causal-student distillation, lookahead/delay-line trade-offs.

*Axis:* `topic`

Mapping body kinematics (speed, jerk, spread, verticality, laterality, Laban effort) to fixture parameters (dimmer, pan/tilt, zoom, strobe, colour). The conductor layer.

*Axis:* `topic`

Using a regression/MSE objective where p(target|input) is multi-modal: the optimal predictor is the conditional mean, a blurred low-energy average no real sample looks like, so held-out R2 is ~0 even when every draw from the true conditional would be acceptable. Diagnosed by an inter-annotator/inter-performer ceiling near zero at the target resolution. Remedy is a generative objective and distributional evaluation, not a different regression target.

*Axis:* `problem`

A trivial or degenerate policy attains the metric's optimum (a metronome maximises beat alignment; persistence maximises level R2; jitter aligns to beats). The metric then cannot separate a working system from a trivial one. Guard: report the trivial policy's score alongside, use the metric as a constraint, carry the claim on a distributional or human metric.

*Axis:* `problem`

Where a result sits on the lookahead axis: strictly causal, bounded lookahead bought with a delay line, or whole-track offline. A score is only comparable to another score at the same point on this axis.

*Axis:* `topic`

replacing hand-written descriptor-to-fixture rules with a learned decoder

*Axis:* `topic`

A number was produced with information the deployed system cannot have at that instant. Covers library defaults that read ahead (centred STFT frames, centred median filters, global top_db clamps), interpolating onto a control grid from a later analysis frame, and any offline fit quoted as if it were online. Distinct from matched-baseline: the baseline may be fine and the FEATURE still illegal.

*Axis:* `problem`
*Axis:* `topic`

stems, per-stem features and their use as conditioning

*Axis:* `topic`

data.name: audio_to_dmx_latency_ms
data.description: Wall-clock from an audio sample entering the causal front-end to the DMX frame that reacts to it, measured on the deployment box with a click-track impulse; reported together with any deliberate lookahead/delay-line L so latency = pipeline + L.

data.name: Companion to pose-stage active coordinate speed ratio
data.description: Median emitted six-head pan/tilt coordinate speed at40Hz in fixedShpongle70-90s. Ratio against unchanged-body pose_stage baseline; movement amount, NOT synchronization or aesthetic preference.

data.name: critic_accuracy_real_vs_beat_trigger
data.description: Accuracy of the audio-light critic at telling the real authored light for a song from beat-trigger light rendered on the same audio, on held-out songs. Real-vs-time-shift accuracy is reported next to it but does not count: a critic that separates shift but not beat-trigger has learned RMS and onsets.

data.name: cue_transition_frechet_distance
data.description: Frechet distance between the look-TRANSITION statistics of a generated cue stream and the authored corpora's (inter-cue interval median and CV, hue jump at cues, value-class change at cues, fraction of cues within 100 ms of a beat / downbeat, cues per minute), reported with a split-half floor of the authored set and a shuffled-donor null.

data.name: Beat-free dance model: paired wrong-audio MSE advantage
data.description: Validation-pilot metric on continuous pose-derived com_speed and vert_bounce_amp at10Hz. TRAIN-standardized truth and predictions are smoothed identically with a centered one-second uniform filter. A fixed next-canonical-song donor and correct audio use identical common prefix length and explicit whole-prefix generation noise. Per seed/song, average generation draws/coaches within recordings then recordings within canonical songs, compute(MSE_wrong−MSE_correct)/MSE_wrong, and average across songs. Undefined/zero denominators stay undefined. No beat grid, event quota or per-prediction scaling.

data.name: Beat-free dance model: normalized motion variation ratio
data.description: Generated/reference mean absolute lag difference in TRAIN-standardized20-dimensional pose descriptors, normalized by frozen TRAIN lag IQR for lags1,5,10,20,40 at10Hz. Ratios aggregated equally by recording within canonical song; undefined reference variation remains undefined. Report alongside audio correspondence to detect nearly constant outputs.

data.name: descriptor_audio_r2_over_dancer_identity
data.description: Per motion descriptor and per timescale (0.1/0.5/2/8 s): held-out-track R2 of an audio-feature model MINUS the R2 of a dancer-identity baseline (one-hot dancer / per-dancer mean), on AIST++ and FineDance. Positive = audio carries information beyond who is dancing; the channel may enter the deterministic block A. Near zero with small inter-dancer r = sample it (block C) or drop it. Reported together with inter-dancer r and the period-locking strength of the channel at tactus/2-beat/bar.

data.name: descriptor_above_6hz_energy_over_corpus
data.description:
Share of a predicted descriptor channel's variance above 6 Hz, divided by the share the real corpus channel has, averaged over held-out clips. 1.0 is the target; above 1 is jitter the body never produced.

The targets are mocap through a 12 Hz zero-phase Butterworth and are physically smooth. A flow head sampled per frame is not, even conditioned on its own previous output: measured 2026-09-04 the sampled block ran 11x to 452x the corpus value (section_energy 116x, space_eff 202x, weight 343x, hand_spread 452x) while the regressed block sat at 0.3-5x. That excess is what crosses the light's visibility threshold and drives light-event-rate-ratio.

data.name: edm_collapse_rate
data.description: Fraction of frames in which the latent dancer's MDV speed falls below the 5th percentile of real dance MDV speed, on out-of-distribution (club/EDM) music. Detects the in-the-wild collapse InfiniteDance documents for AIST++/FineDance-trained generators.

data.name: event_ap_lift_audio_marginal
data.description: Marginal lift in per-song average-precision (AP / base rate) from adding audio features to the rhythm-of-past-changes baseline, for predicting a lighting scene change in the next 1.0 s. 5-fold CV by song. Judged against a circular-shift permutation null that preserves event count and rhythm, so AP's small-sample upward bias cancels.

data.name: event_ap_lift_audio_only
data.description: Per-song AP / base rate for predicting a lighting scene change in the next 1.0 s from audio features alone, no rhythm baseline. 5-fold CV by song.

data.name: event_ap_lift_by_feature_family
data.description: Marginal lift in per-song AP over the rhythm baseline for predicting a lighting scene change, computed separately per interpretable audio feature family (energy / spectral / harmonic / timbre) and for the openl3 learned embedding. Each family judged against its OWN circular-shift null, because families differ in dimensionality and therefore in overfitting bias.

data.name: event_ap_lift_vs_horizon

Period is shared; phase is personal.
